questions.explanationCorrect: Running a simple, high-volume task on the largest model wastes cost and latency. Matching the model to the task, a smaller, faster model, fixes the root cause.
questions.explanationDistractor: Adding more instructions does not address the mismatch between a heavyweight model and a lightweight task; the model choice is the lever.

questions.stem: A genuinely complex, multi-step analysis produces shallow, error-prone results on a small, fast model. What is the most appropriate fix?

options.A: Ask the very same question several more times over on that exact same small and fast model
options.B: Shorten the prompt quite sharply so that there is far less content to confuse the model
options.C: Lower the maximum output length setting that is currently configured for the model responses
options.D: Move to a more capable model (and enable extended thinking) suited to hard reasoning

questions.explanationCorrect: When a task genuinely exceeds a small model's reasoning, the fix is to match the task to a more capable model, and extended thinking, rather than retrying the same underpowered setup.
questions.explanationDistractor: Repeating the prompt on the same small model does not add the reasoning capacity the complex task needs; the model is the constraint.

questions.stem: Every day you correct Claude's tone the same way in a fresh chat. What is the durable fix?

options.A: Put the tone rule in the Project's custom instructions once, so it applies automatically
options.B: Simply keep on correcting the tone by hand in every single new chat, day after day after day
options.C: Accept the off tone as an unavoidable limitation of the tool itself
options.D: Try opening Claude in a different web browser and see if it helps

questions.explanationCorrect: A repeated manual correction is a signal to fix the configuration. Putting the tone rule in the Project's custom instructions solves it once for every future chat.
questions.explanationDistractor: Correcting the tone by hand each day is the endlessly repeated one-off patch that a durable configuration change is meant to replace.

questions.stem: A developer keeps pasting files from a large codebase into chat one at a time to get Claude to make coordinated edits, and it is painful and error-prone. What is the root-cause fix?

options.A: Simply paste the individual code files into the chat one by one, only faster this time
options.B: Use Claude Code, which works directly across the repository, instead of chat
options.C: Paste every one of the files into a single, giant chat message
options.D: Reduce the number of files involved by deleting some of the existing code first

questions.explanationCorrect: The pain comes from using the wrong entry point. Claude Code operates directly on the repository, eliminating the manual file-by-file pasting that chat forces.
questions.explanationDistractor: Pasting everything in one giant message still lacks the repository access and editing workflow that Claude Code provides, and it strains a single conversation.

questions.stem: Claude's answer about a fast-moving topic is confidently out of date. What is the most direct fix?

options.A: Rephrase the very same question using a whole handful of different synonyms
options.B: Ask Claude directly to please try to "be more current" about the topic
options.C: Enable web search so Claude can retrieve up-to-date information
options.D: Switch over to a smaller and faster model just for this one question

questions.explanationCorrect: Out-of-date answers on recent topics stem from the training cutoff. Enabling web search lets Claude pull current information rather than relying on stale knowledge.
questions.explanationDistractor: Asking Claude to "be more current" cannot conjure post-cutoff facts it never learned; it needs a retrieval tool like web search.

questions.stem: Two people give Claude "clean up this text" and get very different results, and neither is what they wanted. What is the root cause and fix?

options.A: The model itself is just inherently inconsistent, so really nothing can be done about it here
options.B: The text that they each handed it is simply far too long for the model to handle well
options.C: They should each simply ask the very same thing several more times
options.D: "Clean up" is ambiguous; specify what to change (grammar, tone, length, formatting)

questions.explanationCorrect: Ambiguous instructions like "clean up" invite divergent interpretations. Specifying exactly which changes you want removes the ambiguity and makes results predictable.
questions.explanationDistractor: The variability is not randomness to accept; it stems from an under-specified request, which precise instructions resolve.

questions.stem: An output got worse after you edited your prompt, but you changed several things at once. What is the best troubleshooting move?

options.A: Revert, then reintroduce the changes one at a time to find which caused the regression
options.B: Go ahead and change even more things all at once, and just hope the overall result improves
options.C: Abandon the whole prompt entirely and just start over from nothing
options.D: Assume the model itself quietly degraded and simply wait a day

questions.explanationCorrect: Isolating variables is core to troubleshooting. Reverting and reapplying changes one at a time reveals exactly which edit caused the regression, so you can fix it precisely.
questions.explanationDistractor: Changing even more at once makes the regression harder to diagnose, compounding the very problem that caused it.

questions.stem: Claude gives wrong answers about your internal process. You are tempted to blame the model, but it was never given the process documentation. What is the real root cause?

options.A: The model is simply and fundamentally incapable of the entire task at hand here
options.B: Missing context: Claude was not given the internal information it needs
options.C: An incorrectly configured temperature setting on the underlying model itself
options.D: The particular time of day at which you happened to ask

questions.explanationCorrect: Wrong answers about private information usually mean the context is missing, not that the model is incapable. Supplying the internal documentation is the fix.
questions.explanationDistractor: Blaming the model's core capability misdiagnoses the problem; Claude simply never received the internal information the answer depends on.

questions.stem: Claude's responses are far longer and more rambling than you need for a quick summary. What is the durable fix?

options.A: Manually delete the unnecessary parts out of each and every single response by hand every time
options.B: Ask it to "be concise" with no further detail and hope for the best
options.C: Specify explicit constraints, for example "at most five bullet points, one line each"
options.D: Switch over to a larger, more capable model for the summaries

questions.explanationCorrect: Rambling output is best fixed by explicit constraints on length and structure. Concrete limits like "five bullets, one line each" reliably shape the response.
questions.explanationDistractor: Editing every response by hand is an endless one-off patch; setting a concrete length constraint fixes the behavior at the source.

questions.stem: A prompt underperforms. Which sequence best reflects sound troubleshooting?

options.A: Immediately switch straight to the biggest, most expensive model available, and then simply move on
options.B: Randomly tweak the prompt wording until something finally sticks
options.C: Blame the model, decide it just cannot do this, and stop using it
options.D: Identify the likely root cause (ambiguous ask, missing context, wrong model or entry point) and fix it

questions.explanationCorrect: Effective troubleshooting diagnoses the specific root cause, ambiguity, missing context, model fit, or entry point, before applying a targeted fix, rather than guessing.
questions.explanationDistractor: Randomly tweaking wording may occasionally help by luck but teaches you nothing and often misses the actual cause, like missing context or a model mismatch.

questions.stem: You discover a prompt tweak that reliably fixes a recurring problem across your team's chats. What is the best way to capture the win?

options.A: Keep the useful prompt tweak to yourself and simply reuse it again yourself the next time around
options.B: Apply the tweak by hand whenever you happen to remember to
options.C: Mention the tweak once in a team meeting and then move on
options.D: Build it into the shared Project configuration so every chat benefits automatically

questions.explanationCorrect: A durable fix belongs in shared configuration. Encoding the improvement in the team's Project makes every future chat benefit automatically, instead of depending on individuals remembering to apply it.
questions.explanationDistractor: Applying the tweak manually whenever you remember is fragile and does not help teammates; building it into shared config makes the fix permanent and universal.
